Hi Liam —

Thanks for the productive QBR last week. Based on your growth trends and the burst events in July, I put together a renewal proposal that consolidates your three monthly tiers into a single higher commit with a predictable burst buffer. Key points in the attached proposal (redwood-proposal-v3.pdf):

- New monthly committed throughput: 1.25M tokens/month (up from current 600k)
- Tier simplification: flatten to one committed band with step-down soft-throttle windows
- Burst allowance: 30% monthly burst cushion, subject to soft-throttle after cushion is exhausted
- Rate changes: consolidated per-token rate of $0.0009 for committed usage, $0.00125 for burst
- SLA: 99.9% uptime for hosted endpoints, with explicit fallback routing to compatible model variant

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick confirmation from procurement that the consolidated rate band works for them
2) If approved, I’ll send a DocuSign with the 12-month term and one optional 6-month auto-extension
3) Ops will provision a burst buffer and update routing policies prior to the effective date

I attached the July usage export so you can see the distribution we used for the proposal. Would you be available for a 20-minute call this week to walk through the burst behavior and the ops runbook?

Vanessa / Aditya —

Quick answers and suggested contract language. Pricing math attached inline:

- Burst measurement: agreed to measure the 30% burst cushion against the monthly committed tokens. We will include a supplemental table showing daily p95/p99 to explain July's two-day events. Aditya: thanks for pulling the day-level peaks.
- Soft-throttle behavior: we recommend the following contract text — "Soft-throttle engages after the monthly committed + burst cushion are exceeded; requests may be queued for up to 30 seconds with a target 95th percentile latency not to exceed 2x nominal latency for text-generation endpoints during soft-throttle windows." This gives StratoApps predictability while protecting shared capacity.
- Top-up and overage: include both an automated overage billing path (at burst rate) and a one-time manual top-up option via the billing portal; language: "Customer may purchase ad-hoc capacity top-ups; absent a top-up, overage will be billed at the published burst per-token rate."

Price sanity check: consolidated committed rate $0.0009/token on 1.25M tokens/month = $1,125/month committed; expected utilization profile suggests effective blended rate ~ $0.00095/token after normal burst usage. Confirm legal ok with auto-topup clause — if not, we can make the top-up manual only.

Ops notes for provisioning before effective date:
- Provision 1.25M token monthly bucket on their dedicated logical tenant
- Attach a 30% burst buffer that maps to a soft-throttle policy; configure fallback routing to secondary region and compatible model variant (gpt-redwood-3-smaller)
- Add tracing hook and tagging for their account to show token-level cost and latency during any throttle events

If everyone is good with the language, Vanessa — send the updated proposal and I’ll get finance to pre-authorize the billing lanes.

Cheers,
